# Steady Growth Marketing

> A Google Ads agency and growth marketing consultancy based in Lakewood, New Jersey, that plans, runs, and optimizes paid search, Google Shopping, Performance Max, and Meta Ads campaigns for e-commerce stores and lead-generation businesses across the United States. Engagements are month to month, clients keep full ownership of their ad accounts and data, and results are reported in revenue and cost per lead rather than clicks.

## Services

- **Google Ads Management**: Search, Shopping, Performance Max and Display campaigns, engineered around margin and cost per acquisition. Includes account restructuring, wasted-spend audits, keyword and bidding strategy, ad copy and landing page testing, and conversion tracking built to survive privacy changes.
- **Meta Ads Management**: Facebook and Instagram paid social for e-commerce and lead generation, optimized toward revenue and qualified leads.
- **E-Commerce Consulting**: Google Merchant Center setup and disapproval fixes, product feed optimization, Shopping and Performance Max campaign architecture, and product-page and checkout conversion optimization.
- **Lead Generation**: Landing page design and split testing, funnel and form friction analysis, audience targeting, and lead-quality scoring fed back into bidding so campaigns optimize toward closed business, not form fills.
- **Recruitment Advertising for ABA Providers**: Google Ads campaigns for ABA and behavioral health clinics hiring BCBAs, BCaBAs and RBTs. Commute-radius geographic targeting rather than city lists, single-role landing pages, negative keyword lists that exclude certification and salary research traffic, and offline conversion tracking through phone screen, interview, offer and start of employment so cost per hire can be compared against agency placement fees.
- **Self-Storage Advertising**: Google Ads management for self-storage operators. Campaigns structured by unit size and current vacancy rather than one budget for the whole facility, facility-level radius targeting so multi-site operators do not bid against themselves, brand defense against aggregator sites and national operators, call tracking, and offline conversion tracking that reports cost per completed move-in rather than per reservation.
- **Amazon Advertising Management**: Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display for sellers and brands, measured on total advertising cost of sale (TACoS) against total Amazon revenue rather than a single campaign's ACoS. Brand and non-brand separated in reporting, search-term reports harvested into their own targets and negated where they don't convert, acceptable ACoS set per product from contribution margin, listing conversion-rate work ahead of bid changes, budget driven by Buy Box status and inventory depth, and Amazon read alongside Google and Meta on blended spend and revenue.
- **Home Care and Senior Care Marketing**: Google Ads and Meta Ads for home care agencies, built around whether the service radius carries enough local search volume to support paid search at all. Where it does, search covers condition-specific terms, payment questions and brand defense against franchises and paid referral networks; where it does not, Meta carries lead generation by reaching the adult child before the search happens. Qualifying friction in lead forms, call coverage matched to the ad schedule, and offline conversion tracking through qualified conversation, in-home assessment and start of care with authorized hours, so campaigns optimize toward clients rather than form fills. Caregiver recruitment advertising runs as a separate account.
- **Legal and Personal Injury PPC**: Google Ads management for law firms, built around the fact that legal is the most expensive category in paid search and a budget below what the category costs produces almost nothing rather than proportionally less. Budget set backwards from case value and lead-to-signed rate, practice areas chosen by fundability rather than case size, Local Services Ads and the license and background verification they require, intake response time and after-hours coverage as the largest controllable variable, offline conversion tracking through qualified consultation and signed retainer with case type attached, brand defense against lead sellers and directories, and account structure that keeps ad copy reviewable against state bar advertising rules.
- **RV, Boat and Vehicle Storage Marketing**: Paid search for vehicle storage at self-storage facilities and dedicated lots, run separately from unit storage because the demand curve, the searcher and the competitor set all differ. Budget paced against vehicle seasonality rather than facility occupancy, campaigns split by space length band instead of unit size, the attributes that decide the sale surfaced as search terms (covered or enclosed, surface, power at the space, dump station and wash bay, access hours, pull-through versus back-in), a wider targeting radius than unit storage warrants, and move-ins tracked with space length and seasonal versus annual tenancy attached.
- **Analytics & Reporting**: GA4 and Google Tag Manager implementation, enhanced and server-side conversion tracking, attribution modeling, and dashboards tied to revenue rather than sessions.

## Industries served

E-commerce and DTC brands, Amazon sellers, self-storage operators, nonprofits and institutions, home care and senior care agencies, home services (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, remodeling), law firms and personal injury practices, professional services (accounting, consulting), healthcare and dental practices, B2B and SaaS, and multi-location retail.

## How the agency works

- Month-to-month engagements; no long-term contracts.
- Clients own their ad accounts, billing, and historical data.
- Clients work directly with the strategist running their account.
- Typical minimum ad budget: about $3,000 per month.
- Measurable movement in cost per acquisition usually within 30 to 45 days; compounding growth typically in months two through four.
- A free, no-obligation marketing audit is offered: a review of account structure, wasted spend, conversion tracking accuracy, and competitive positioning, delivered as a list of specific opportunities.
